solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 15 and his TV platoon roughed ma about?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of roughed and ma are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sitcom character and his platoon knock someone's mother around.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is MY OLD MAN, i.e. Dad: Dad's Army was a BBC sitcom about a wartime volunteer defence platoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The platoon in the TV comedy Dad's Army belonged to Britain's wartime volunteer defence force.

clue.text: Why best man turned up dependent on the turkey?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the reason someone is a best man: a pal wed

explanation.surface: A puzzled wedding guest asks why the best man showed up relying on the turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Why best man?' is answered 'pal wed', written backwards. 'Dependent' is used in its literal sense of hanging down.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of loose skin hanging from a turkey's throat is its wattle, literally something hanging from the bird.

clue.text: Starting with spinner, finishing with weaver", as the answer goes

parts.note: starting with something means beginning from it
a top is a toy that spins
finishing with means going up to, so to
Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A description of a textile process, from spinning yarn to weaving cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a down entry, so it is read in the direction the phrase describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A down answer is read vertically, beginning at the upper square and ending at the lowest one.

clue.text: Poet bristling at quotas in trunk

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for trunk

parts.note: the trunk of the body is the torso

indicators.note: bristling suggests agitation, so the letters of at quotas are stirred up

explanation.surface: A poet gets angry about quotas while sitting in a trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bristling' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal. Torquato Tasso wrote the epic Jerusalem Delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth-century Italian writer of Jerusalem Delivered was an epic poet.

clue.text: Disease whose deficiency would leave Her Majesty repeating?

indicators.note: repeating means the whole unit appears twice in a row
the vitamin letters leave the royal letters between them, so the royal letters sit inside

parts.note: the disease is caused by lack of vitamin B1, written B and I
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A riddle about an illness whose lack would leave the Queen stuck repeating herself.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the deficient B1 from each half and only ER ER is left: B-ER-I twice.
explanation.definitionFit: This illness is the classic vitamin deficiency condition, caused by lack of thiamine.

clue.text: Double check climbing plant

parts.note: with check, double means two checks; the first is vet, to examine closely
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: An instruction to double-check a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double check' asks for two words for check: VET and CH.
explanation.definitionFit: This leguminous plant climbs by tendrils and is grown as fodder.

clue.text: Source of howl, bark and jabber

definitions.meaning: a dog, an animal that howls and barks
one who jabs, a fighter in the ring

explanation.surface: A list of noisy sounds: howling, barking and chattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jabber' looks like chatter but is one who throws jabs.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a breed of dog and a pugilist who throws punches.

clue.text: In Queens, shot missing the police force assessor?

indicators.note: In places the attempt and the police inside the two queens

parts.note: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a queen; two queens give it twice
a shot is a go, an attempt
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: In the New York borough of Queens, a shooting goes unsolved by the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queens' is not the New York borough but ER twice; the shot and the Met go between them.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures the work or force exerted, as on a rowing machine.

clue.text: "Kinky" romance — can she have a go?

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of romance can she are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a woman should try a racy romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take a risk or attempt something with uncertain success.

clue.text: Tee shot, two things found by St Anne's dog

indicators.note: shot means got rid of, so the letter goes

parts.words: two things found by St Anne's
parts.note: Lytham St Annes is a seaside resort, so beside St Anne's lie the sea and Lytham
tee is the letter T

explanation.surface: A golfer's tee shot at Royal Lytham and St Annes, with a dog nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: Lytham St Annes is a Lancashire seaside town whose Royal Lytham golf course hosts the Open; the golf surface hides that 'Tee' is just T.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh terrier breed is a small white wire-haired hound.

clue.text: Stratford-on-Avon chippy: "A selection of preserves"?

definitions.meaning: a carpenter created by Stratford's Shakespeare: Peter, in A Midsummer Night's Dream; chippy is British slang for a carpenter
a fruit commonly made into jelly or jam

explanation.surface: A Stratford fish-and-chip shop advertising a range of jams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chippy' in Britain means both a chip shop and a carpenter; here it is the carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter of that name is Shakespeare's carpenter, and the hard fruit is usually eaten as a preserve.

clue.text: Write adaptation of Peter Pan up, securing first place

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the rearranged letters hold the other piece
an adaptation reworks the original, so the letters of Peter Pan up are rearranged

parts.note: first place is the top

explanation.surface: A writer is told to set down an adaptation of Peter Pan and top the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adaptation of' is the anagram signal and 'securing' the container signal: the rearranged PETER PAN UP holds the first-place word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to start writing, literally applying a nib to a sheet.

clue.text: Holiday: fancy a bite? This?

parts.note: Whit, short for Whitsun, is a church holiday

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborate or reworked, so the letters of a bite are shuffled

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker is offered a snack and asks if this is it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like 'would you like' but rearranges A BITE into EBAIT. The whole clue also defines: the little fish is a seaside snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny young fish, fried whole, make a popular holiday snack.

clue.text: "Terror-stricken order: Quit Hill!", as the answer goes

indicators.note: stricken means struck through, so the other pieces strike into the word for terror

parts.note: terror means fright
OM is the Order of Merit
quit, in the past tense, means left
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A frightened soldier gets the command to abandon the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an across entry, so it is read in the direction the phrase describes; 'stricken' is the container signal. OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An across answer reads horizontally, starting at the western square and ending at the eastern one.

clue.text: Raving mad — only tailgating motorway van driver!

indicators.note: tailgating means following close behind, so the scrambled letters come after the motorway letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

indicators.note: raving means wild, so the letters of mad only are thrown about

explanation.surface: An enraged motorist yells at a van driver tailgating on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the British music-hall song 'My Old Man Said Follow the Van', about a family flitting with the furniture van.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old music-hall song, Dad goes with the removal van, so he is a cheeky 'van driver'.

clue.text: In which (hint) you will find a clue

definitions.text: In which (hint) you will find a clue

parts.words: In which (hint) you will find a clue
parts.note: the word hint sits inside parentheses, and every crossword letter count is shown in the same punctuation

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter promising a hint on where to find a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue demonstrates itself: '(hint)' and '(5,8)' are both enclosed this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Parentheses, the curved punctuation marks, are where a crossword shows each enumeration.

clue.text: Club chocolate bar in radio ads

indicators.note: radio ads are only heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: KitKat is a well-known wafer chocolate bar

explanation.surface: A club advertising a chocolate bar on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kit-Cat Club was an early-eighteenth-century London Whig dining club.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a celebrated literary and political society of Georgian London.

clue.text: His brother made a mess of his inheritance

definitions.text: His brother made a mess of his inheritance

parts.words: His brother made a mess of his inheritance
parts.note: in Genesis, Esau sold his birthright to his twin for a mess of pottage, a bowl of stew

explanation.surface: A sibling squandered the family inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' means a dish of food, not a muddle: Esau traded his birthright for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch bought his elder twin's birthright with a bowl of stew.

clue.text: What transports a doctor back in time is …

definitions.text: What transports a doctor back in time is …

indicators.note: in puts the article and the turned doctor inside time plus is
back means the doctor's abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: An unfinished sentence about the time machine in Doctor Who.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal and 'in' the container signal. The whole clue also describes Doctor Who's time-travelling police box.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor's time-travelling police box in the BBC series Doctor Who carries him through time.

clue.text: Where reactions happen, conversely, in wine-butts etc

indicators.note: conversely says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the words that follow, spanning wine-butts etc

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wine merchant contemplating the reactions inside casks and barrels.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft missed that 'in' is the hiding indicator; 'conversely' then reads the hidden letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemical experiments are carried out in this small glass laboratory tube.

clue.text: A threesome fixed by descendant of ancient Egyptian countryman

indicators.note: fixed by means held in place by, so the trio sits inside

parts.note: a Copt is an Egyptian Christian, descended from the ancient Egyptians
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A threesome being put right by an Egyptian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed by' is the container signal: the trio is held by the Egyptian Christian. Copts are Egypt's native Christian community.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow citizen of one's own nation is a compatriot, someone of the same land.

clue.text: Port city's first guidebook covers Day One

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of city's
covers means wraps round, so the guidebook letters go around the others

parts.note: an A-Z is a London street atlas
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A city's first guidebook covers day one of a visit to a port.
explanation.walkthrough: A-Z is the standard British street-map book; it wraps D I.
explanation.definitionFit: This Andalusian city is an ancient Atlantic seaport in southern Spain.
